statement: Our result on algebraic dependence testing in AM ∩ coAM gives further indication that a randomized polynomial time algorithm for the problem exists. Studying the following special case might be helpful to get an idea for designing better algorithms. Given quadratic polynomials f1 , . . . , fn ∈ F2 [x1 , . . . , xn ], test if they are algebraically dependent in randomized polynomial time [34]. As indicated in this paper, approximate polynomials satisfiability, or equivalently testing zero-membership in the Zariski closure of the image, may have further applications to problems in computational algebraic geometry and algebraic complexity. We know that HN is in AM over fields of characteristic zero, assuming GRH [24]. Can we solve AnnAtZero (or APS) in AM for fields of characteristic zero assuming GRH [22]? This would also imply a better hitting-set construction for VP.
